contractRevision.description: Active contract revision when this attempt was emitted; absent means the original locked contract (revision 0). Optional and additive — a pre-existing trace that omits the field still validates, and a missing field is interpreted as revision 0 by downstream readers. Non-negative integer so revision-scoped accounting cannot be tricked by a negative or non-integer value.

class.description: How the clarifier disposed of the detected gap: resolved silently with a framework default, defaulted but overridable by the user, or surfaced as a blocking question. camelCase ASCII.

gapClass.description: Catalog label for the kind of ambiguity detected (e.g. scope_ambiguity, target_of_n). snake_case ASCII because these are human-facing catalog labels, not protocol discriminators; the pattern keeps multi-word labels legible.

payload.description: Class-specific detail kept open here: the shape varies by class (e.g. resolution/source for selfResolved, assumedDefault/rationale for blocker). The producing role owns the inner shape; the schema does not constrain it.

round.description: Which clarification round detected the gap. 1 is the initial round; 2 and 3 are the two permitted evolution rounds, so the budget is enforced at the schema edge as well as in the orchestrator.

action.description: What the user did at the draft-preview menu, including the auto-approve-on-timeout fallthrough so the unattended path is auditable. camelCase ASCII.

payload.description: Action-specific detail kept open here: e.g. evolutionText for evolved, editor/duration/chars for edited, empty for the rest. The producing role owns the inner shape.

round.description: Which round the interaction terminated, matched to the same 1-3 budget as clarifierFinding so a reader can correlate the two series within a round.

errorCode.description: F2 error code, PascalCase ASCII Type-like name (e.g. UntrustedOverlay, PathEscape). Distinct from the camelCase trace discriminators by design.

eventType.description: Event-class discriminator. The ten values are the v1 known set; readers tolerate unknown values per the forward-compatibility contract (see the schema-level description). camelCase ASCII.

independentReview.description: One independent-review event emitted by the contract-free reviewer role after a generator attempt. The payload is a lightweight summary (the full findings live in the sprint-{N}-independent-review-{attempt}.json artefact); this event marks 'a review happened' in the run trace so consumers can locate it without parsing the artefact file. Deliberately distinct from agentAttempt because the reviewer is off-budget — counting an agentAttempt here would mis-fire the sprint-budget guard.

payload.description: Lightweight reviewer summary inlined on the event itself (small and integral, same precedent as safetyHalt.payload). The full reviewer findings live in the sprint-{N}-independent-review-{attempt}.json artefact; this object only carries the counts and the verdict so a reader can scan the trace for the review's outcome without opening a sibling file.

attemptLetter.description: Single uppercase ASCII letter identifying the generator attempt this review covered ('A' for the first attempt, 'B' for the second, and so on). Matches the {attempt-letter} placeholder in the sibling artefact filename so the two are joinable without ambiguity.

contractRevision.description: Active contract revision when this review ran. Non-negative integer (0 is the original locked contract); mirrors agentAttempt.contractRevision so revision-scoped queries against the trace are consistent across event classes.

sprintNumber.description: Sprint this review belongs to. Positive integer; sprints are 1-indexed throughout the framework.

summary.description: Counts of findings by severity tier plus the count of findings the orchestrator dropped (e.g. a command finding whose reproductionCommand did not reproduce). All four counters are required and non-negative so a reader can do arithmetic on them without nullability checks.

verdict.description: Single-word outcome of the review. 'clean' means zero surviving findings of any severity; 'findings' means at least one finding survived the false-positive guard (a renegotiation round may follow, gated by the cap).

disposition.description: Set on sprint-end milestones; the run/sprint outcome.

milestone.description: Sprint-level transition label. camelCase ASCII; new values stay on v1 per the additive-discriminator rule.

relativePosixPath.description: Relative POSIX path from the trace root. No leading separator and no '..' traversal segments.

roleId.description: Agent role identifier, kebab-case ASCII (e.g. gan-generator).

payload.description: Class-specific shape owned by the triggering spec (A1 owns loopDetected; A2 owns scopeViolation). T1 reserves the extension point and does not constrain the payload's inner shape.

safetyClass.description: Discriminator within the safetyHalt class. The v1 known values are loopDetected, scopeViolation, future; readers tolerate unknown additive values per the forward-compatibility contract. camelCase ASCII.

sequenceNumber.description: Monotonic non-negative integer, no gaps within a run.

sha256Hex.description: SHA-256 hash, hex-encoded lowercase, exactly 64 chars. No sha256: prefix (bare hex per T1 field encodings).

timestamp.description: RFC 3339 UTC timestamp with millisecond precision. The pattern enforces the encoding directly (the repo's pinned ajv runs strict:true with no ajv-formats, so format:date-time is not used): the trailing Z and the .mmm fraction are required and local timezones are forbidden.

errorPayload.description: The F2 error payload, preserved verbatim ({ code, message, file?, field?, line?, ... }).

preflightAbort.description: A pre-spawn preflight halt: the framework refused to spawn the first sub-agent because a session-level invariant did not hold. The four documented strings are the only fields — operator state (hook contents, probe env, stdin envelope) is deliberately excluded so telemetry cannot leak it.

errorSubReason.description: Closed set of per-stage discriminators paired with `preflightStage`. The `confineHook` stage emits `noGanRunDirAwareness` (probe ran the hook to completion and the hook refused the GAN_RUN_DIR write) or `projectHookMisconfigured` (the hook is not a runnable bash script). New preflight stages extend this set; the framework's schema then validates the pairing.

description: JSON Schema (draft-07) for a single ClaudeAgents run-trace event (T1). Every event carries the common envelope (sequenceNumber, eventType, timestamp, runId) plus the class-specific fields selected by the eventType discriminator. The oneOf below is the v1 KNOWN set of event classes. Forward-compatibility / additive-evolution contract (T1 F1.2): a NEW optional field, a NEW discriminator value within an existing class (e.g. a new safetyHalt.safetyClass or orchestratorMilestone.milestone), and a NEW event-class type ENTIRELY all stay on v1 and DO NOT bump the schema version. A field RENAME or a SEMANTIC change of an existing field forces run-trace-v2. Because additive changes stay on v1, the schema's oneOf cannot itself accept future-unknown event classes; the v1 READER (not this schema) is responsible for tolerating both an unknown discriminator value within a known class AND an unknown event-class type, skipping such an event with a structured warning rather than erroring. The envelope is therefore intentionally open (no envelope-level additionalProperties:false) so future optional fields validate against v1.
title: ClaudeAgents run-trace event, v1
